extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners, regulated parties (sponsors/applicants), policy analysts, and stakeholders submitting or reviewing notice-and-comment rulemaking on public charge inadmissibility
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural guidance in DHS's public charge rule (inadmissibility under INA sec. 212(a)(4)) including sponsor affidavit requirements, exemptions, definitional rules, decision procedures, and the economic/regulatory-analytic calculations used in the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge inadmissibility (INA sec. 212(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of inadmissibility on public charge grounds under INA sec. 212(a)(4) (8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References Field Guidance and prior rulemakings (e.g., 1999 Field Guidance; 2019 and 2021/2022 rules). The determination may be made by predicting likelihood of becoming a public charge based on the totality of the alien's circumstances at the time of application (citing Matter of Perez and Field Guidance). See related regulations at 8 CFR 212.22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totality of the circumstances analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: "The determination of whether an alien is likely to become a public charge ... is a prediction based upon the totality of the alien's circumstances at the time he or she applies for an immigrant visa or admission to the United States."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited sources (Field Guidance, Matter of Perez). DHS notes empirical data (e.g., that no cases were ultimately denied based solely on totality under the 2019 Final Rule) and discusses how totality interacts with the regulatory factors in 8 CFR 212.22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Support / Sponsor financial requirements (INA sec. 213A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must demonstrate means to maintain income per INA sec. 213A (8 U.S.C. 1183a), and when required the applicant must submit Form I-864, Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A of the INA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS notes that a sponsor demonstrates means by presenting Federal income tax returns or by demonstrating significant assets of the sponsored immigrant or sponsor if available. Citations to 8 CFR 213a.2(c)(2)(ii), 213a.2(c)(2)(iv), 213.1(a)/(c). Time-burden estimates and opportunity-cost calculations for completing I-864, I-864A, I-864EZ, and I-864W are provided (hours and dollar estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms, fees, and paperwork burdens (I-485, I-693, I-864 family)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and cost burdens associated with immigration forms relevant to public charge review: Form I-485 filing fee, Form I-693 medical exam (Form I-693), biometrics fees, and associated opportunity costs and travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS provides specific calculations: Form I-485 filing fee $1,140; opportunity cost per applicant using wage and benefits multipliers; biometrics fee $85; estimated hours for form completion and biometrics collection; example calculations summing annual costs (e.g., $715,613,873 total annual cost for filing Form I-485 using stated assumptions). References to source documents (form instructions and PRA supporting statements) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and scope of "receipt of public benefits" and long-term institutionalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions used to determine what counts as receipt of public benefits and which institutional services qualify as long-term institutionalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS states it is replacing the term 'institutionalization for long-term care at government expense' with 'long-term institutionalization' to better describe covered services and duration; references to Social Security Act section 1905(a) for institutional services and to 8 CFR 212.21/212.22 for benefit receipt definitions. Cross-references to prior Federal Register discussions are cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt classes from public charge review
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain classes of noncitizens are exempt from public charge review (e.g., refugees, asylees, Afghans and Iraqis employed by U.S. government, special immigrant juveniles, Temporary Protected Status recipients, trafficking and crime victims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations to INA secs. 207, 208, 209, and to the regulatory text (8 CFR 212.22(a) and (c)); specific examples and prior program references (e.g., Operation Allies Welcome) are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory provisions and citations (8 CFR 212.21, 212.22, 212.23, 213.1, 213a.2, 103.3, 103.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule relies on and interprets specific regulatory provisions in the Code of Federal Regulations relevant to public charge inadmissibility, sponsor obligations, and decision procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent cross-references to 8 CFR sections (e.g., 212.22(a)-(e), 212.21, 212.23, 213.1(a)/(c), 213a.2) are provided; the rule points readers to USCIS Policy Manual chapters and other Federal Register notices for procedural and interpretive guidance (e.g., requests for evidence and notices of intent to deny per 8 CFR 103.3(a)(1)(i) and USCIS Policy Manual Vol. 1, Part E, Ch. 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision procedures, evidence requests, and appeal processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural standards for decisions, including the use of Requests for Evidence (RFEs), Notices of Intent to Deny (NOIDs), and applicable appeal/argument procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 8 CFR 103.3(a)(1)(i), USCIS Policy Manual Vol. 7, Part A, Ch. 11 (Decision Procedures), and USCIS Policy Manual Vol. 1, Part E, Ch. 6 (Requests for Evidence and Notices of Intent to Deny). Also references historical 'Oral Argument and Appeals' Federal Register material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of OMB Circular A-4 and regulatory impact analytic methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS uses OMB Circular A-4 guidance for conducting the regulatory impact analysis (cost–benefit methodology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple citations to OMB Circular A-4 (Sept. 17, 2003) and to the 2019 Final Rule Regulatory Impact Analysis; economic assumptions such as benefits-to-wage multipliers and wage-rate calculations are applied following these methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical data handling and exclusions in analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: How DHS treats data for analytic purposes, including exclusions of anomalous years and manual review of denial cases to determine causation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: exclusion of FY2019–FY2021 data due to anomalies; manual review to identify cases denied under section 212(a)(4) and to determine whether denials resulted solely from totality analysis; citation of USCIS internal analyses and external data sources (Defense Manpower Data Center, BLS, GAO, academic reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting and calculation rules for population subject to public charge review
rubrics_metrics.description: Method for calculating the population subject to public charge review (e.g., total adjustment of status applicants minus exempt populations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS provides arithmetic examples: Total Population Applying for Adjustment of Status − Total Population Seeking Adjustment of Status that is Exempt from Public Charge Review = Total Population Subject to Public Charge Review. Example calculation for FY2018: 704,407 − 180,179 = 524,228.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor demonstration via assets or tax returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor may demonstrate means to maintain income by presenting Federal income tax returns or by demonstrating significant assets of the sponsored immigrant or sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites INA sec. 213A(f)(1)(E) and 213A(f)(6) and 8 CFR 213a.2(c)(2). DHS explicitly lists acceptable documentary evidence (tax returns, asset demonstration) as ways to show sponsor capacity.
